dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4701.text: A crooked mouth, 𤺉. Formed from 疒, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4702.text: Unable to speak. Formed from 疒, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4703.text: A lump on the neck. Formed from 疒, with 嬰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4704.text: Swelling of the neck. Formed from 疒, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4705.text: To tremble. Formed from 疒, with 又 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4706.text: Accumulated blood. Formed from 疒, with 於 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4707.text: Abdominal pain. Formed from 疒, with 山 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4708.text: An ailment of the lower abdomen. Formed from 疒, with abbreviated 肘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4709.text: Fullness. Formed from 疒, with 𡚤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4710.text: An illness causing one to bend forward. Formed from 疒, with 付 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4711.text: A curved spine. Formed from 疒, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4712.text: Qi moving contrary to its course. Formed from 疒, 屰 and 欠.

shuowen:4713.text: Unsettled qi. Formed from 疒, with 季 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4714.text: A wind ailment. Formed from 疒, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4715.text: A swelling. Formed from 疒, with 畱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4716.text: A small swelling. Formed from 疒, with 坐 indicating the sound. Another explanation: clustered swellings, 族絫.

shuowen:4717.text: An abscess. Formed from 疒, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4718.text: An abscess. Formed from 疒, with 麗 indicating the sound. Another explanation: emaciated and dark. Read like 隸.

shuowen:4719.text: A swelling. Formed from 疒, with 雝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4720.text: An extraneous growth of flesh. Formed from 疒, with 息 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4721.text: A dry sore. Formed from 疒, with 鮮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4722.text: Itching or scratching. Formed from 疒, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4723.text: An itching eruption, 疥. Formed from 疒, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4724.text: A woman’s ailment. Formed from 疒, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4725.text: A malignant illness. Formed from 疒, with abbreviated 蠆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4726.text: Heat and cold recurring with intervals of rest. Formed from 疒 and 虐; 虐 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4727.text: A recurring fever with heat. Formed from 疒, with 占 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The Marquis of Qi had an itching eruption, then a fever.”

shuowen:4728.text: A fever recurring every two days. Formed from 疒, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4729.text: An abdominal ailment, 疝. Formed from 疒, with 林 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4730.text: An ailment of the rear. Formed from 疒, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4731.text: Numbness or obstruction, 痹. Formed from 疒, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4732.text: An illness caused by dampness. Formed from 疒, with 𢌿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4733.text: Qi failing to reach the feet. Formed from 疒, with 畢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4734.text: A swollen lump from exposure to cold. Formed from 疒, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4735.text: One side withered or paralyzed. Formed from 疒, with 扁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4736.text: Qi in the shins and swelling of the feet. Formed from 疒, with 童 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Both frail and swollen.”

shuowen:4737.text: An ailment causing lameness. Formed from 疒, with 盍 indicating the sound. Read like 脅, or like 掩.

shuowen:4738.text: Injury from a beating. Formed from 疒, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4739.text: Beating injuries, 疻痏. Formed from 疒, with 有 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4740.text: A wound splitting open. Another explanation: 疾𤼒, an ailment; this gloss is uncertain. Formed from 疒, with 巂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4741.text: Skin peeling off. Formed from 疒, with 冄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4742.text: Pain. Formed from 疒, with 䢉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4743.text: Injury. Formed from 疒, with 夷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4744.text: An injury or scar. Formed from 疒, with 般 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4745.text: A callus or scar. Formed from 疒, with 艮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4746.text: Stiffness and contraction. Formed from 疒, with 巠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4747.text: An ailment involving movement. Formed from 疒, with abbreviated 蟲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4748.text: Emaciated. Formed from 疒, with 叜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4749.text: A heat illness. Formed from 疒 and 火.

shuowen:4750.text: An illness from exertion. Formed from 疒, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4751.text: A yellowing illness. Formed from 疒, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4752.text: Labored breathing in illness. Formed from 疒, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4753.text: Pain. Formed from 疒, with 否 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4754.text: A vessel ailment, 脈痬; the self-referential gloss is uncertain. Formed from 疒, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4755.text: To run wildly. Formed from 疒, with 术 indicating the sound. Read like 欻.

shuowen:4756.text: Weary. Formed from 疒, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4757.text: A flaw. Formed from 疒, with 𠂔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4758.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 氏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4759.text: Weakened by illness. Formed from 疒, with 及 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4760.text: A severe or intense sound; the gloss 劇聲 is uncertain. Formed from 疒, with 殹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4761.text: Debilitated by illness. Formed from 疒, with 隆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4762.text: The people all becoming ill. Formed from 疒, with abbreviated 役 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4763.text: Children’s convulsive illness, 瘛瘲. Formed from 疒, with 恝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4764.text: An ailment of horses. Formed from 疒, with 多 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Weary are the white horses with black manes.”

shuowen:4765.text: A sore on a horse’s shin. Formed from 疒, with 兌 indicating the sound. Another explanation: about to be injured.

shuowen:4766.text: To treat or cure. Formed from 疒, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4767.text: Long illness. Formed from 疒, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4768.text: Chu people call the toxicity of medicine 痛瘌. Formed from 疒, with 剌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4769.text: Joseon calls the toxicity of medicine 癆. Formed from 疒, with 勞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4770.text: To recover. Formed from 疒, with 𢀩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4771.text: To lessen. Formed from 疒, with 衰 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to diminish.

shuowen:4772.text: Illness healing. Formed from 疒, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4773.text: To recover from illness. Formed from 疒, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4774.text: Not intelligent. Formed from 疒, with 疑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4775.text: To cover. Formed from 一 hanging down. All characters in this group are formed from 冖.

shuowen:4776.text: A binding, used to bind the hair; the general name for caps and ceremonial crowns. Formed from 冂 and 元; 元 also indicates the sound. A crown has regulated forms, hence 寸.

shuowen:4777.text: To accumulate. Formed from 冂 and 取; 取 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4778.text: To set down a cup of wine as an offering. Formed from 冂, with 託 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “The king lodged three nights, sacrificed three times and offered wine three times.”

shuowen:4779.text: A double covering. Formed from 冂 and 一. All characters in this group are formed from 𠔼. Read like 苺 in 艸苺苺.

shuowen:4780.text: To join together. Formed from 𠔼 and 口.

shuowen:4781.text: The image of a curtained canopy. Formed from 𠔼; 㞢 is its ornament.

shuowen:4782.text: To cover. Formed from 𠔼 and 豕.

shuowen:4783.text: Headwear of children and the Man and Yi peoples. Formed from 冂; 二 is its ornament. All characters in this group are formed from 冃.

shuowen:4784.text: The crown of grand officers and above, with a deep projecting board, hanging pendants and cords with floss ear-stoppers. Formed from 冃, with 免 indicating the sound. In antiquity the Yellow Emperor first made it.

shuowen:4785.text: A helmet. Formed from 冃, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4786.text: To go forward while covered. Formed from 冃 and 目.

shuowen:4787.text: To violate and seize. Formed from 冃 and 取.

shuowen:4788.text: Twice. Formed from 冂; further analysis is missing. The Changes says: “Give Heaven three and Earth two.” All characters in this group are formed from 㒳.

shuowen:4789.text: Twenty-four zhu make one liang. Formed from 一 and 㒳, equal division; 㒳 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4790.text: Even or level. Formed from 廿, the number of the five phases; twenty divisions make one 辰. 㒳 conveys evenness. Read like 蠻. The numerical explanation is uncertain.

shuowen:4791.text: The knotted cords with which Paoxi fished. Formed from 冂, with the lower part depicting a net’s crossing strands. All characters in this group are formed from 网. The classics now use the clerically transformed 䍏.

shuowen:4792.text: A net, 䍑. Formed from 网, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4793.text: A net. Formed from 网, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4794.text: A net. Formed from 网 and 繯; 繯 also indicates the sound. Another explanation: to tie up.

shuowen:4795.text: A net. Formed from 网, with 𣫭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4796.text: A net. Formed from 网, with 巽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4797.text: To travel all around. Formed from 网, with 米 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “They spread into its difficult places.”

shuowen:4798.text: A fish-catching device. Formed from 网, with 卓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4799.text: A fishing net. Formed from 网, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4800.text: A bamboo fishing net. Formed from 网 and 非. Qin used 罪 for the graph 辠.
